text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Hosni Mubarak said feasibility studies on the giant New Valley project were done 20 years ago and they proved that the area is suitable for agriculture using the surplus of Nile water. Mubarak said those who oppose the project do so because they want to shake confidence in any project because they do not want progress or else they have wrong information.
- At an expanded ministerial meeting today, President Mubarak will review final details of the New Valley project in the light of the report presented by the prime minister.
- Boutros Boutros-Ghali returned to Egypt after the end of his term at the United Nations. Foreign Minister Amr Moussa met him at the airport and said Mubarak would meet him today.
- Mubarak spoke to Palestinian President Yasser Arafat by phone yesterday. Arafat briefed Mubarak on developments in Israeli-Palestinian negotiations.
- Mubarak also received a phone call from Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh on Arab and Middle East issues.
- Mubarak has become a grandfather. Heidi, wife of his son Alaa, gave birth to a baby boy yesterday.
- It has been decided to sell tranches of shares in 14 companies in the first quarter of this year under the privatisation programme and another 20 will be sold in full.

- President Mubarak in his televisiuon interview said: "Ganzouri's government has a long task ahead to complete economic reform... Because of security and stability I could not find a hotel bed in Hurghada or Sharm el-Sheikh."
- Towards the end of this week, Mubark will give the starting signal for the New Valley project.
- Mubarak said in television interview: "Our aim is to improve the standard of living."
- The ministerial committee will visit the south of the valley within hours. It has reviewed the timetable for building the irrigation canal and the pumping station.
- General John Shalikashvili, chairman of the U.S. joint chiefs of staff, will arrive in Cairo today for talks with Chief of Staff Magdi Hattata.
